data.claim: Four of five edits are data (fixture, redact tables, coherence EXEMPT, fragment) and can be read by AST and inserted textually; the fifth is code.
data.falsifier: check on the tree reports a missing edit for a kind that passes the four ratchet tests
data.mechanism: AST scan of the tables, textual insert after the literal opener
data.probe: uv run python scripts/event_kind.py check; then the four ratchet test files
data.question: Can one script list and apply the five hand edits of a new event kind?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED: check agrees with the four ratchet tests on the tree (303 passed)
ran the fleet brief for this item (D-small-files honoured: script 8 KB, test 4 KB)
scripts/event_kind.py check/add, lenient read_log, tests/test_event_kind_scaffold.py; 399 selected tests passed

chunk_findings.detail: When a kind already has a `LOG_TEXT_FIELDS` entry, `add` still emits a *second* line for that same kind key. `text = [n for n in args.text if n not in text_fields.get(kind, ())]` (line 155) filters out fields already listed, but it does not consider that the kind key itself is already present, and `_insert` splices the new line directly after `LOG_TEXT_FIELDS: ... = {`, i.e. *before* the pre-existing entry. A Python dict literal with a duplicate key keeps the last occurrence, so the pre-existing (later) entry wins and the newly requested text field is silently dropped. Concrete input: a kind `lease.waiting` already mapped to `("reason",)`; run `scripts/event_kind.py add lease.waiting --why "..." --text detail`. The script prints `redact: LOG_TEXT_FIELDS lease.waiting ['detail']`, but the written literal is `{ "lease.waiting": ("detail",), ... "lease.waiting": ("reason",), ... }`, `literal_eval` (and the imported module) yields `("reason",)`, and the `check` pass that `main` runs immediately afterwards re-reads the file and reports `redact: field 'detail' is neither LOG_TEXT_FIELDS nor a lookup` — the exact failing-test round the tool exists to avoid. The stated contract ("it never edits an entry that exists") is also violated.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/event_kind.py:155-157 (`add`, LOG_TEXT_FIELDS insert)

chunk_findings.detail: `add` is not atomic: the fixture is rewritten at lines 149-153 (and `LOG_TEXT_FIELDS`/`LOG_VERBATIM_FIELDS` are spliced at 157/167) *before* the `--lookup` spec is validated at lines 162-163 and before the `--exempt` length check at lines 171-172. Input `scripts/event_kind.py add foo --why "w" --field x=str --exempt "too short"` raises `SystemExit("--exempt: say why in more than 20 characters")` only after the fixture entry for `foo` and the redact edits have been written to disk, leaving the repository half-scaffolded with no coherence entry or fragment; the user must hand-undo, which reintroduces the multi-round failure mode the script is meant to remove. Likewise `--lookup x` (no `=WHY`) aborts at line 163 with the fixture already modified.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/event_kind.py:141-172 (`add`, write-before-validate ordering)

chunk_findings.detail: The dedup for lookup fields only checks the on-disk set `taken`, never the `pairs` being accumulated, so a repeated option inserts the same `(kind, name)` key twice: `--lookup f=why1 --lookup f=why2` writes two identical-key lines into `LOG_VERBATIM_FIELDS`, and `literal_eval` (last-wins) keeps only `why2`, silently discarding the first reason.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/event_kind.py:164 (`add`, --lookup dedup)

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that `check x.new` lists all five hand edits, but its loop is `("handler", "fixture", "coherence", "fragment")` and omits `redact`. Given the input `x.new` (a kind with no edits anywhere), if `event_kind.py check x.new` never emits the `x.new: redact:` line, this test still passes because only the other four substrings are asserted and the nonzero return code alone does not prove the redact edit was reported. That leaves the redact-listing capability, one of the five edits this change exists to surface, unverified at the only positive test for the “lists all of them” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_event_kind_scaffold.py::test_a_kind_with_no_edits_lists_all_of_them

chunk_findings.detail: The tolerance is applied only to the parse step, not to the read step. `p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` is evaluated in the `for` header, *outside* the `try`, so a half-written shard can still kill `--write` — with a different exception than the one the change targets. Concretely: if the worktree's `.ddflow/events/*.jsonl` is being appended to by a running ddflow while `--write` reads it, the bytes on disk can end in the middle of a UTF-8 sequence (the writer's 8 KiB block buffer can flush on a boundary that falls inside a multi-byte character, which is easy when payloads contain non-ASCII message text). `read_text` then raises `UnicodeDecodeError` before any line reaches `Event.from_json`, the `except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)` never runs, and `python tests/test_event_upcasters.py --write` still dies — exactly the failure mode the intent says must be tolerated. (Similarly `FileNotFoundError` if a shard is rotated away between `glob` and the read.) Reading with `errors="replace"` / opening and iterating inside the `try`, or wrapping the whole per-file read, is needed to actually deliver "tolerant of a half-written shard".
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_event_upcasters.py:103 (`read_log`)

chunk_findings.detail: The lenient path swallows far more than the torn-tail JSONDecodeError that motivated it: `KeyError` and `TypeError` from `Event.from_json` on a *complete* line are also skipped, and `_write` then goes on to overwrite the committed fixture with what it did observe. Input: a shard containing a well-formed JSON line for a kind whose upcaster chain does not yet know a newly required key (the very workflow this feature targets) — `from_json` raises `KeyError`, the line is printed to stderr and dropped, and line 660 writes `tests/fixtures/event_kinds.json` without that kind's fields while exiting 0. Before this change that line aborted the run *before* `FIXTURE.write_text`, so the fixture could not be silently corrupted; now the regenerated fixture can be missing kinds, and the omission surfaces later as an unrelated-looking coverage/upcaster failure. Restricting the skip to the final (possibly unterminated) line of each shard, or to `json.JSONDecodeError` only, keeps the intended tolerance without letting schema bugs rewrite the fixture.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_event_upcasters.py:657 (`_write` → `read_log(logs, lenient=True)`)
